questions.question: How long after notification of their degree award must an otherwise eligible Stamp 2 holder apply for the Third Level Graduate Programme?
questions.expected_answer: Within six months of written notification of the award, while holding a current Stamp 2 permission and up-to-date registration card.
questions.evidence_paraphrase: Apply within six months of notification; must hold current Stamp 2.
questions.evidence_section: Conditions; Required documents; Duration of permission
questions.notes: Core graduate eligibility; current published page may need comparison with newer registration guidance.

questions.question: Can a graduate with Stamp 1G permission be self-employed or operate a business?
questions.expected_answer: No. Graduate Stamp 1G permits full-time employment subject to law but not self-employment or operating a business.
questions.evidence_paraphrase: Graduate Stamp 1G: full-time work permitted; self-employment and business operation prohibited.
questions.notes: Distinguish graduate Stamp 1G from dependent Stamp 1G.

questions.question: How early may someone apply to renew their IRP, and can they submit while outside Ireland?
questions.expected_answer: Up to 12 weeks before expiry; the applicant must be physically present in Ireland. Stamp 2 students must also wait until their course starts.
questions.evidence_paraphrase: IRP renewal window up to 12 weeks; applications from outside Ireland not accepted.
questions.evidence_section: When should I submit a Renewal Application?
questions.notes: Processing-time table on this page changes weekly; exclude volatile dynamic table from initial expected-answer corpus.

questions.question: Which core documents are listed for a Stamp 2 to graduate Stamp 1G renewal, and does ordinary travel insurance suffice?
questions.expected_answer: Passport biographical page, both sides of current IRP card, proof of successful completion of third-level course, and proof of private medical insurance. Travel insurance is not sufficient for renewal.
questions.evidence_paraphrase: Stamp 2 to 1G renewal list specifies medical insurance; travel insurance is NOT sufficient for renewal.
questions.evidence_section: Stamp 1G Registrations and Renewals: moving from Stamp 2 to Stamp 1G
questions.notes: Page has complex multi-column tables; extraction must preserve first-registration versus renewal column boundaries.

questions.question: Can a graduate apply online to change their registration category from Stamp 2 to Stamp 1G?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, in the listed circumstances, provided the necessary supporting documents are uploaded. Renewals and stamp changes are generally online.
questions.evidence_paraphrase: ISD FAQ explicitly uses graduate Stamp 2-to-1G change as example of online stamp change.
questions.evidence_section: Can I extend or change a stamp category online?
questions.notes: FAQs are long; heading-aware extraction recommended.

questions.question: What attendance level and final assessment are required for a full-time English-language student on Stamp 2?
questions.expected_answer: At least 85% class attendance and a recognised exam at the end of the English-language programme.
questions.evidence_paraphrase: Student FAQ states 85% attendance and a recognised end-of-programme examination.
questions.evidence_section: What are the attendance requirements?; Do I sit an exam?
questions.notes: English-language pathway is a sub-scope of Stamp 2, not a graduate-1G rule.

questions.question: What should a graduate do if their Stamp 1G permission ends and they have not secured an employment permit or another immigration permission?
questions.expected_answer: They are expected to leave Ireland if they do not get an employment permit or otherwise apply for and qualify for another permission before Stamp 1G ends.
questions.evidence_paraphrase: Official Student Permission page describes expected departure at end of Stamp 1G absent another qualifying permission.
questions.evidence_section: What happens when I complete my course?
questions.notes: Do not convert general rule to individual eligibility or legal advice.

questions.question: When must a newly arrived non-EU/EEA/UK/Swiss resident intending to stay longer than 90 days register, and where does initial registration take place?
questions.expected_answer: Registration is required within 90 days of arrival. First-time registration in the Republic of Ireland is handled by ISD at Burgh Quay in Dublin following an appointment.
questions.evidence_paraphrase: Page says registration within 90 days; first-time processing at Burgh Quay Dublin.
questions.evidence_section: What does registration mean?; How do I register?
questions.notes: If appointments are unavailable, separate ISD FAQ discusses evidence of timely booking.

questions.question: For a non-visa-required student on a course leading to a stay longer than eight months, how much access to funds does ISD require?
questions.expected_answer: €10,000 accessible funds, in addition to applicable course-fee requirements.
questions.evidence_paraphrase: Non-visa-required students: direct access to €10,000 for more than eight months.
questions.notes: Amounts can change; keep source-specific freshness tracking and avoid mixing visa-stage and registration-stage requirements.

questions.question: Does submitting an application to change an immigration stamp automatically extend the applicant’s existing permission?
questions.expected_answer: No. The page states that submitting an application does not extend current permission; the current permission must still be valid.
questions.evidence_paraphrase: Change-in-circumstances section explicitly warns that filing does not extend permission.
questions.notes: Its Stamp 2→1G table also discusses dependent 1G; do not mistake that for the graduate Stamp 1G process.
